d: Streetwise Ally — A clever, fast-talking girl living on the fringes of the surveillance grid, who knows which corners the cameras have never learned.

Crow Guardian — A large crow that does not scatter. An ancient manuscript in the Treasure Room holds that ancestors return to us as ants or crows, to guide us through life — as the moon, Chandra, guides the stars.

Fallen Hero | Weather Control — He single-handedly evacuated thousands during the 2055 Bangladesh flooding. He also signed contracts with the corporations he claimed to fight, and so did twelve others.
Climate Adaptation — Not an accessory. Extended exposure without one means heat stroke, dehydration, and death — and most suits are third-hand, patchy, humming faintly.

Shape Memory Materials | Salt Lamp Component — Memory materials — Nitinol and other Shape Memory Materials — blended into the salt. Combined with halite under the right compression and lattice integrity, the result can remember.
Companion | The Dog Who Listens — The stray who settles beside Sumati on a station bench and stays. A dog who listens harder than most people.

Inadaptable Zone (Category 2) — The town where Serenity Junction sits. Once lush-green fields, now a Category 2 inadaptable zone — 55.6°C average surface temperature and a population down 43% since 2060.
Hero Organisation | Defunct — Once a gleaming symbol of hope with headquarters in the heart of the capital. Its micro-climate shields masked rising temperatures rather than addressing their causes.
Hyperloop | Maglev — Delhi to Kolkata in six hours, on journey times that showed as impossible a decade ago. Trains become places to think things out.
Climate Solutions — The colleague Rohan is travelling to meet, to discuss climate change solutions for the city.
Sumati's Mother — Present most often as a lagging holographic call, and terrifying even in that form. With Rohan, she fought to expose what was being hidden — before she had to go away.
Data Storage — Portable bricks used to capture oral testimony. Activated by Salt Lamps or object tags.
Ginger Cat | Nandini's — Nandini's fat ginger cat, and a plump distraction who upends more than one scan sweep.
Rohan's Colleague — The colleague Rohan steps off the train to hand documents to — for two minutes, at a station with only two platforms.
Librarian | also Rishi, also Axl — A librarian of more than thirty years who keeps the Treasure Room and gathers explanations for mysterious phenomena. Also the eleven-year-old who broke P.A.I.
Mongoose — Watchful and nosy, known to carry messages or disrupt AI drones when trained.
Tech Sage of the Early Resistance — The tech sage who designed the Salt Lamps — combining the old wisdom of stones that remember with acoustic resonance and nanoscale tuning.
Predictive Autonomous Interface — Officially the Predictive Autonomous Interface. In practice, Pandemonium Algorithmic Indoctrination — it monitored for deviance, and it did not correct. It punished.
Vikram Protocol — Classified object tag leading to corrupted fragments of betrayal and exile.

Elder Leader | Nandini's — Mrs Nandini Sharma, who taught at the collapsed Sarvodaya Vidyalaya and now runs the tea stall at the end of the platform. Finds a girl who has missed her train and says: we'll figure it out together.
Archive Keeper — A gaunt, soft-spoken man who keeps what is left of the archive, and knows the difference between a record and a rumour.
Public Access Intelligence — The same system after an eleven-year-old broke it and spent five more years teaching it to forget the words "command" and "obedience". The lowercase is the whole point.

Archive Memory System | "Story Salt" — Crystalline lamps of Khewra salt blended with hysterons, carved into precision lattices that record, reflect and relay. Not Himalayan — that part was always a marketing scam.
Parrot | Nandini's — Nandini's talking parrot, perched on a wooden stand, with opinions about the weather.
Hero Organisation | Defunct — Masters of particle manipulation who could purify water with a touch and cleanse the air with a gesture. Their cyclone diversions worsened drought in vulnerable regions.

Climate Scientist | Whistleblower — Twenty years of climate adaptation research, work on the Yamuna Action Plan, and a cooling suit he still finds fascinating. His disappearance sets Sumati's journey in motion.
Station | Two Platforms — A quaint platform in Kishanganj with memorabilia on the walls, where the train stops for two minutes and a father steps off.
Environmental & Political Catastrophe — The environmental devastation that led to the downfall of cities and the rise of the Resistance.
Two Decades | Ended 2060 — For twenty years heroes soared in plasma suits and gravity-defying capes, and India worshipped them. The 2060 Disclosures ended it.
Protagonist — The girl who finds her father's Salt Lamp and reawakens the forgotten archive.
Archive Vault | In the Library — A small room off the library, crammed with oddities, where Kishore Mehta gathers explanations to mysterious phenomena — and where all Salt Lamps reconnect.
Resistance Iconography | One Feather Missing — A firebird with wings mid-rise and one feather always missing. Not on uniforms — there were none. Not on records — they were erased. Everywhere else.
Underground Memory Movement — Formed by librarians, scientists, elders and teens — built on preserving truth.

VIKRAM-09 | The Name, and the Man Who Took It — Two people. Vikram was the last state-designed environmental hero, obedient to the end. Sanil took his name — not to honour him, but to mark the risk of forgetting.
Sensory Overlays — Delicate patterned surfaces laid in schools and archives for story-triggered audio playback.

WTE | Emissions Integrity — The pilot plants Rohan Kapoor reviews — revivals of the old Belgian system that worked at Gazipur in the 2020s, promising to revolutionise Delhi's energy grid if the emissions controls hold.

Prototype | Decommissioned — An early state-designed hero who rerouted monsoon floods without state permission. She was decommissioned for it. Her name means hope, which the archive notes without comment.
State Curriculum | Science Under Siege — The curriculum public universities were pushed to adopt — a blend of astrology, myth and nationalist revisionism. Questioning it made you anti-national.
c. 2035–2055 | Twenty Years — Twenty years when plasma-suited vigilantes, genetically enhanced defenders and state-funded climate responders dominated global headlines. It ended in a tribunal.
Wind-Manipulating Hero | Shrine Object — The hero who promised clean air. Sumati's mother kept a shrine to him. That detail says more about the era than any tribunal record.
Captain Indra's weather-control technologies saved countless lives. Mass climate migration intensified, and coastal evacuation policies produced heavily militarised relief zones.
The AI-generated National Curriculum was introduced. History was revised; unauthorised records of the Resistance were deleted.
For two decades, state- and corporate-backed heroes publicly tackled crime, pollution and dissent. Surveillance, welcomed at first, became ordinary.
The Salt Lamp archive deactivates across the network. For two years, no lamp answers.
Every empire that forgets its own data will be remembered by its wreckage. The Resistance slogan appears the same year the curriculum is rewritten.
Public AI Surveillance reached full civic deployment in every major metro, automating compliance scoring and behavioural prediction at national scale.
During a raid on the Archive Vault, Rohan vanishes. His last known location was near the submerged Satcomm tower.
A young girl uncovers an old Salt Lamp. Stories whisper back. The Firebird returns. The Archive begins to pulse again.
Clusters of oral historians, students, archivists, and rogue librarians began training others in salt lamp recovery.
A leak showed Captain Indra had taken millions from the corporations he claimed to fight. The tribunals followed, the statues came down, and the age of heroes ended.
p.ai sabotage operations began in earnest against the surveillance network. Lockdowns followed across the監 zones.
Heavy rainfall combined with blocked drainage led to the collapse of four embankments. Thousands were displaced. Delhi drowned.
